problem: Most VLMs rely on RGB only and must implicitly infer 3D geometry, so they cannot guarantee metric alignment and generalize poorly across scenes when asked where to act in 3D. Prior depth-aware VLMs use depth as an auxiliary cue, and existing point-prediction work covers surface-attached targets but not free-space (air) targets.
motivation: Grasping, placement and navigation all reduce to deciding where to act in 3D, and RGB-D sensors are widely available on robots. Feeding structured depth directly into a pre-trained VLM could give metric grounding, but adding a new modality to a VLM is non-trivial.
key_idea: Add an explicit depth-token stream to Qwen3-VL through a duplicated depth backbone and depth delimiter tokens, and decode (u,v,Z) point lists for touchable (surface) and air (free-space) targets.
insight: Depth input helps a lot. RGB-only drops touchable accuracy from 0.790 to 0.676-0.698 and depth MAE rises from 17.2 to about 190-227 mm; on air points RGB-only reaches DirPt of only 0.20-0.31, against 0.49-0.51 with depth. The dedicated (dual) depth backbone and the special depth tokens each add gains (supplementary A10-A18 vs Ours3). SpatialBot-style depth encoding beats naive Depth-3ch, and XYZ point-cloud input gives better metric precision on air points but worse direction correctness and much worse touchable accuracy (0.443).
method: Unified target representation: every target is a (u,v,Z) triplet (pixel coordinates in [0,1000), depth in mm), serialized as plain text and learned by token prediction with no binning.

SpatialPoint-Data engine: 1.9M touchable QA pairs made by lifting RoboAfford 2D annotations with Depth Anything 3 monocular depth, plus 0.72M air-point QA pairs from DINO-X detections lifted to 3D, over 26 camera-frame directions (direction, between-object, body-length queries, optionally with metric offsets).
Depth encoding: the single-channel depth map is converted to a 3-channel uint8 image following SpatialBot so it is compatible with the vision tokenizer.

Dual backbones: the RGB vision backbone is duplicated with separate parameters as a dedicated depth encoder on the same patch grid; the depth tokens are wrapped in <dpt_start>/<dpt_end> and concatenated with RGB and text tokens in one causal sequence.

Two-stage training: Stage 1 trains only the depth backbone with 10x learning rate while everything else is frozen; Stage 2 unfreezes the full model for joint fine-tuning with AdamW and cosine decay on mixed touchable and air data.

SpatialPoint-Bench and metrics: touchable points are scored by 2D accuracy inside the GT region mask plus depth MAE; air points by DirPt (30° cone or between-cylinder with 10 cm radius, plus occupancy exclusion), MetPt@5cm, FullPt and MeanErr, all conditional on relation correctness.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-VL-Instruct-4B with an added duplicated depth vision backbone (fine-tuned)
setting.training_data: SpatialPoint-Data: about 1.9M touchable QA pairs (from RoboAfford with Depth Anything 3 depth) plus 0.72M air-point QA pairs (DINO-X + estimated depth); 1 epoch by default, with extra 1-3 epochs on the air subset
setting.observation: RGB image + depth map (monocular-estimated depth for training and benchmark; RGB-D sensor in real robot)
setting.action_space: predicted camera-frame 3D target points as (u,v,Z) text lists, executed by the robot's own controllers
setting.privileged: none at inference; benchmark ground truth uses monocular depth estimates as reference

numbers.extra: trained on SpatialPoint-Data with monocular depth as input

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmarks; the real-robot results are qualitative only (videos/figures).
results: On RoboAfford-Eval, SpatialPoint reaches 0.790 overall touchable accuracy versus 0.741 for RoboBrain 2.5 and 0.503 for Qwen3-VL-4B, with depth MAE of 17.2 mm versus 217.9 mm for RoboBrain 2.5. On air points, DirPt is 0.507 and MeanErr 6.81 cm versus 0.080 and 30.3 cm for RoboBrain 2.5. Zero-shot real-robot demos cover arm pick-and-place, mobile navigation/manipulation and a long-horizon package-reordering task.
limitations: Relies on monocular depth estimates for training data and evaluation references, which may degrade on textureless or reflective regions.
Air-point performance is still modest (DirPt about 0.51, FullPt about 0.16) and it does not handle dynamic scenes or trajectory-level planning.
Real-robot results are only qualitative demos with no quantitative success rates, and the benchmark is self-constructed (small touchable bench of 338 queries).
